gdpr_card_body: Download everything we store about you, or deactivate your account. Deletion anonymizes your identity immediately and purges personal side content within 30 days.
gdpr_delete_confirm_body: This deactivates your account and anonymizes your data. This cannot be undone.
terms_accounts_body: You are responsible for your account and its activity. One account per person; sharing accounts or submitting on behalf of someone else is not allowed. Accounts of users under 16 require parental consent or school-mediated enrollment.
terms_conduct_body: No abuse: attacking the platform, attempting to read other users' data, or circumventing judge limits. During rated contests, solutions must be your own work — see the contest rules published with each contest.
terms_content_body: Code you submit stays yours; you grant the platform the non-exclusive right to display your submissions (e.g. post-solve solution browsing) and verify them for plagiarism. Editorial and forum text you write is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 so the community can reuse and translate it with attribution.
terms_availability_body: The service is provided as-is. We run daily backups and test restores, but we do not guarantee uninterrupted availability; judge results may be re-evaluated if a defect is found.
privacy_what_body: Your account data (username, email, role), your submissions and their judge results, forum posts and votes, problem ratings and scratch runs. Everything is stored on our own infrastructure; we run no third-party analytics or advertising trackers.
privacy_cookies_body: One session cookie pair (httpOnly access + refresh tokens) keeps you signed in — it is not readable by page scripts and expires with your session. There is no tracking cookie, ad cookie or social pixel.
privacy_rights_body: From your profile you can export all of your data as a downloadable JSON file, or delete your account: deletion deactivates it immediately, anonymizes your identity, and purges personal side content within 30 days. Judge history (verdicts and standings) is retained in anonymized form for the integrity of the public record.
privacy_minors_body: Self-serve accounts require the information-society consent age (16 in Romania). Younger students join through school-mediated classroom enrollment under the school's lawful basis, with profiles non-public by default.

support_intro: The platform is free for students and teachers, and it stays that way. If it helps your class, your club or your olympiad preparation, here is how you can keep it running.
support_donate_body: WebCoder is free for students and teachers. Donations cover hosting, the judge infrastructure and the bilingual content work. Write to us and we will send the current donation channel — we publish a donor wall on request.
support_sponsor_body: Companies and organizations can sponsor a rated round or a school olympiad: your name and logo appear on the contest page and standings (attribution only — the contest stays free for everyone). Codeforces-style sponsor rounds are the sustainable model for a community judge.
support_school_body: Schools and county olympiads can run private contests on WebCoder (windowed, personal timers, gradebook export). This is currently free while the platform is in its community phase; a paid hosting tier with an SLA is planned only after the legal and fiscal groundwork (invoicing, registration) exists.
support_no_payments_note: Note: this page processes no payments. Donation channels and any future paid hosting tier will launch with proper invoicing and legal terms — until then, everything on WebCoder is free.

faq_q3: How does the online judge work?
faq_a3: You submit your solution code, and our judge compiles and runs it against hidden test cases. You receive a verdict (Accepted, Wrong Answer, Time Limit Exceeded, etc.) within seconds.

accessibility_standard: We aim to conform to WCAG 2.1 level AA. Every page in the interface is scanned automatically on each change (the axe-core accessibility gate in our continuous integration), and a change that introduces a critical or serious violation does not ship.
accessibility_keyboard: The whole submission flow — finding a problem, writing code in the editor, submitting and reading the verdict — is operable by keyboard alone. Focus is always visible, and pages expose a skip link to the main content.
accessibility_screenreaders: Problem pages, standings tables and forms use semantic landmarks, labels and table headers so screen readers can navigate them. Colour is never the only signal: verdicts carry text, and rating colour bands are always accompanied by numbers.
accessibility_contrast: The interface palette is tested for contrast at the AA ratio on both light and dark surfaces.
accessibility_feedback: If something on WebCoder is hard or impossible for you to use, write to us and we will treat it as a bug: accessibility@webcoder.example. Feedback from teachers and students using assistive technology drives this page.
accessibility_intro: WebCoder is built for schools and students, so it has to work for everyone. This page states what we commit to and how it is enforced — not an aspiration, a gate in our pipeline.
ai_policy_intro: The rating ladder only means something if the solves are real. These rules apply to every rated contest on WebCoder; registering for one means you accept them.
ai_policy_own_work: Submissions during a rated contest must be entirely your own work. Using generative AI (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini or similar) to produce, debug or complete a solution during a rated round is cheating.
ai_policy_no_sharing: Do not share solutions, hints or test observations with other participants while a rated contest is running, and do not publish them before the round ends.
ai_policy_one_account: One account per person. Multi-accounting in rated contests (including entering a division you are not eligible for) is cheating.
ai_policy_tools: Allowed: the platform editor, its starter templates, and scratch runs. Not allowed: external AI assistants, collaboration tools, published solutions of the same problem, and other people — in the room or online.
ai_policy_enforcement: After each rated contest we review solve patterns and run similarity checks. Confirmed violations mean disqualification from the round, rollback of the rating it produced and, for repeated offenses, loss of the account. Judgements are made by the organizers; you can appeal by email.
ai_policy_practice: Outside rated contests — practice, editorials, community discussions — AI tools are yours to use for learning. The restrictions above exist only to keep the rating ladder honest.
judge_docs_intro: Every submission runs isolated in a sandbox with no network access, a per-language time/memory budget and per-test evaluation. The table below is the live language registry — the exact toolchains the judge runs, not documentation that can drift.
judge_docs_limits: Time limits are per test and multiplied per language (for example Python gets 3x, Java 2x and a memory floor); output is capped; runtime errors are reported with their signal. Problems may override the defaults — the effective limit is shown on each problem page for your selected language.
contribute_intro: WebCoder is bilingual because contributors make it bilingual. Teachers: writing problems here is professional development — you get a spec, a review and structured feedback, and your class gets problems in both languages.
contribute_step_spec: Write to the published spec: a bilingual statement (RO canonical, EN mirror), the input/output format, limits, subtasks when the problem is written with them, and the reference solution. The problem form and its validation enforce the spec mechanically.
contribute_step_tests: Provide tests that match the statement (samples are public, the rest hidden), a custom checker when the answer is not exact text (the testlib-compatible exit-code protocol), and — for interactive problems — the interactor. The stress runner lets you cross-check your solution against a brute force before submitting.
contribute_step_review: Submissions go through the DRAFT → PENDING → APPROVED queue. A verifier reads the statement, runs the tests and returns structured feedback; you iterate until it is approved. That feedback loop is the training: it is how the campion teacher-authors got good.
contribute_step_reward: Approved problems, community editorials and articles earn contributor honor — the separate ladder that recognizes the people who build the bank, not just the people who solve it.
